    <h2>Table of spherical codes</h2>
    <h3>Maintained by <a href="https://cohn.mit.edu">Henry Cohn</a></h3>
    <p>This data is archived at <a href="https://hdl.handle.net/1721.1/153543">https://hdl.handle.net/1721.1/153543</a>. If you cite the table, please refer to <a href="https://hdl.handle.net/1721.1/153543">that data set</a>, not this web page.</p>
    <p>A spherical code is a configuration of points on the surface of a sphere, with the goal of maximizing the minimal angle between the points. The following table lists numerically optimized codes, with cases that are known to be optimal marked with &ast;. Each entry links to coordinates for the code. Along with references, in some cases the table lists the minimal polynomial of the cosine of the minimal angle, in which case a code with this exact angle has been proved to exist.</p>
    <p>The table is limited to 32 dimensions and 1024 points, with a few exceptions. It omits cases that have been systematically solved, namely dimensions below three and <i>n</i>-dimensional codes with at most 2<i>n</i> points (see R.&nbsp;A.&nbsp;Rankin, <cite>The closest packing of spherical caps in <i>n</i> dimensions</cite>, Proc. Glasgow Math. Assoc. <b>2</b> (1955), 139–144, doi:<a href="https://doi.org/10.1017/S2040618500033219">10.1017/S2040618500033219</a>). The entries labeled &ldquo;needs more optimization&rdquo; have not fully converged to a local optimum, while most of the others probably have. There are two records listed in Ericson and Zinoviev's book (<cite>Codes on Euclidean spheres</cite>, North-Holland Mathematical Library <b>63</b>, North-Holland Publishing Co., Amsterdam, 2001) that I have not included below: for 80 points in 7 dimensions, their construction describes only 78 points, and for 1024 points in 16 dimensions, I am unable to get their construction to work.</p>
    <p>You can access a plain text table <a href ="/plain">here</a>, which includes some polynomials too large to fit below,  and upload additions or improvements <a href ="/upload-code">here</a>.</p>

      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Dimension</th>
          <th>Number of points</th>
          <th>Cosine of minimal angle</th>
	  <th>References and notes</th>
        </tr>
